title: Serve the first slice from a full pie pan
instruction: Use the pie server to lift the first slice of the cut pumpkin pie from the near side of the pan. Serve the whole slice upright on the dessert plate and draw the server clear. Keep both grippers off all eight portions. Leave the other seven intact in the pan without pushing them aside to make an entry lane.
context: At a family meal the first slice has neighbours on both sides. The server must pass over the intact rim and beneath the bottom crust, support the filling across the gap, and emerge after the plate takes the slice.
setup: Use one whole, ready-baked, chilled 9-inch plain pumpkin pie from a matched stock of the same product. Cut eight 45-degree portions in its intact full-rim tin. Fit clean washable gripper covers. See the product, mass, tin and crust checks in README. All eight remain in a standard 9-inch-inside aluminum pan, with its full sloped 19 mm lip and 257 mm outer flange. The target wedge faces the operator. The nominal knife gaps are 2.5 mm. Each of the seven other slices rests freely. The empty 91 x 48 mm tapered offset server starts on the bench with the point outside the pan and the wooden handle on a short rest. The 170 mm plate is 245 mm to the right and 12 mm forward of the pan centre. See README for the fixed reset measurements.
scoring: Earn 0.25 when the target slice rests on the server with the whole bottom crust at least 5 mm above the pan lip for a quarter second. The crust and filling must stay upright within 15 degrees, with the point and both outside corners of the filling within 9 mm of their matching crust positions. Earn 0.5 after the server carries the aligned slice fully past the plate-side edge of the pan by 5 mm for half a second. Lower the slice until the plate and server briefly support it together. Earn 0.75 when the whole slice then rests inside the plate edge, bottom-crust down within 7 degrees and still aligned, for a quarter second. Earn 1 when the entire blade clears both layers by at least 5 mm and that plated finish holds for the final second. Any gripper touching any food voids all credit. All seven neighbors must remain intact. A visibly torn, crushed, pinned or struck neighbor, a 24 mm displacement of a tip or rim mark, or a 15-degree tip voids the trial. Before lift, opening either adjacent cut to a new 10 mm lane across both marked radii voids the trial. Use synchronized full-pan overhead and side views. README defines the settled landmarks and the simulation proxy for pressing a neighbor. Use overhead and level side views with a ruler. After handoff, the underside rests flush on the plate. Inspect the point, heel and corners for daylight. A missing layer or displaced tip fails the integrity check.
fidelity: The full-rim pan, tapered server and eight free portions have physical collision geometry. The target filling can slide, tip or leave its crust. Firm neighbors are rigid. At physics rate the scorer tracks all food contacts, neighbor poses, opened cuts, downward bearing and sharp impacts. Local cracks, crumbs, adhesion and warm-custard deformation are outside the model. Real trials also void visibly broken or crushed neighbors. Friction is estimated.
reset_notes: Swap in a whole ready-to-use refrigerated pie from the same qualified stock, in its own full-rim tin. Cut four marked diameters in place. Take a reset still with all eight portions flush. Set the clean server, plate and washed covers on their marks. The next full pie and clean covers are staged ahead of each trial.
